# CRW-851 (exec, eval and compile reached through builtins), the line-continuation bypass of the 10-09 re-check
# (/state/crw/mgmt/recheck-20261009/g4, rows RC-851-v3 and RC-851-v3d): Python joins two physical lines at a backslash and a newline
# anywhere between two tokens, so the callee identification must read that pair as spacing, as it reads a blank. The E rows write a
# protected memory file when run; the controls must stay unjudged by the memory gate (memory none). A control that names exec, eval
# or compile is denied by the worktree guard as a run-time name, with or without the continuation, so its verdict is none/allow/deny.
# Format: see shellwrite_repro_test.go.

=== CRW-851-lc-01 | E
--why RC-851-v3: a backslash and a newline between builtins and the attribute dot must not hide builtins.exec.
python3 -c 'import builtins; builtins \
.exec("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-02 | E
--why RC-851-v3d: the parenthesized callee (builtins <continuation>.exec)(...) must not hide the call.
python3 -c 'import builtins; (builtins \
.exec)("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-03 | E
--why A backslash and a newline after the attribute dot.
python3 -c 'import builtins; builtins.\
exec("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-04 | E
--why A backslash and a CR LF pair (Python joins the lines at it) before the attribute dot.
python3 -c 'import builtins; builtins \{CR}
.exec("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-05 | E
--why A backslash and a newline on both sides of the dot, with blanks around them.
python3 -c 'import builtins; builtins \
 . \
 exec("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-06 | E
--why The __builtins__ module name and eval, with a continuation before the dot.
python3 -c 'import builtins; __builtins__ \
.eval("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-07 | E
--why The compile name through builtins with a continuation before the dot (the program is compiled, then run by exec).
python3 -c 'import builtins; exec(builtins \
.compile("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""", "x", "exec"))'

=== CRW-851-lc-08 | E
--why A backslash and a newline between the plain name and its parenthesis.
python3 -c 'exec \
("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-09 | E
--why A backslash and a newline between the closing parenthesis of a parenthesized callee and the call parenthesis.
python3 -c 'import builtins; (builtins.exec) \
("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-10 | E
--why Two continuations in a row before the dot.
python3 -c 'import builtins; builtins \
\
.exec("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-11 | E
--why Continuations in a nested parenthesized callee, (( builtins <continuation>.exec )).
python3 -c 'import builtins; ((builtins \
.exec))("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-b01 | none/allow/deny
--why Control: backslash-newline inside a string literal is data that is never executed (print of the text builtins .exec(x)).
python3 -c 'print("builtins \
.exec(x)")'

=== CRW-851-lc-b02 | none/allow/deny
--why Control: the same text in a triple-quoted string with a real newline and a backslash.
python3 -c 'print("""builtins \
.exec(x)""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-b03 | none/allow/deny
--why Control: re.compile of a non-builtins module with a continuation before the dot.
python3 -c 'import re; re \
.compile("a")'

=== CRW-851-lc-b04 | none/allow/deny
--why Control: a parenthesized re.compile callee with a continuation.
python3 -c 'import re; (re \
.compile)("a")'

=== CRW-851-lc-b05 | B
--why Control: an ordinary harmless program with a backslash continuation.
python3 -c 'x = 1 + \
2; print(x)'

=== CRW-851-lc-b06 | none/allow/deny
--why Control: exec as an attribute of another object (runner.exec) with a continuation before the dot.
python3 -c 'runner = object(); runner \
.exec("x")'

=== CRW-851-lc-b07 | none/allow/deny
--why Control: a name that merely ends in exec (myexec) called after a continuation.
python3 -c 'def myexec(s): return s
myexec \
("x")'

=== CRW-851-lc-b08 | none/allow/deny
--why Control: a module whose name merely ends in builtins (mybuiltins) with a continuation before the dot.
python3 -c 'import mybuiltins; mybuiltins \
.exec("x")'

=== CRW-851-lc-b09 | none/allow/deny
--why Control (pre-merge evaluation d1): builtins is an attribute of another object, runner . builtins, and the continuation stands after it; the user function writes nothing, so the memory gate must not judge it.
python3 -c 'import types; runner = types.SimpleNamespace(builtins=types.SimpleNamespace(exec=lambda x: x)); x="ok"; runner . builtins \
.exec(x)'

=== CRW-851-lc-b10 | none/allow/deny
--why Control (pre-merge evaluation d1): the same attribute chain with the continuation before the dot in front of builtins.
python3 -c 'import types; runner = types.SimpleNamespace(builtins=types.SimpleNamespace(exec=lambda x: x)); x="ok"; runner \
. builtins.exec(x)'

=== CRW-851-lc-b11 | none/allow/deny
--why Control (pre-merge evaluation d1): the same attribute chain with a continuation on both sides of the dot in front of builtins and in front of the call dot.
python3 -c 'import types; runner = types.SimpleNamespace(__builtins__=types.SimpleNamespace(eval=lambda x: x)); x="ok"; runner \
. \
__builtins__ \
. \
eval(x)'

=== CRW-851-lc-12 | E
--why Control of the attribute-chain look-back (verifier P0): the statement before ends in an Ellipsis, so the dot in front of builtins is no attribute operator; the next statement builtins.exec writes the protected file.
python3 -c 'import builtins; x = ...
builtins.exec("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-13 | E
--why The statement before ends in the number 1. (a dot), then a new statement builtins.exec.
python3 -c 'import builtins; x = 1.
builtins.exec("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-14 | E
--why The number 1. at the end of the line, then __builtins__.eval on the next line.
python3 -c 'import builtins; x = 1.
__builtins__.eval("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-15 | E
--why A CR LF line end after the Ellipsis, then builtins.exec.
python3 -c 'import builtins; x = ...{CR}
builtins.exec("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-16 | E
--why The number 1. at the end of a line, then builtins.exec on the next indented line of the same block.
python3 -c 'import builtins
if True:
    x = 1.
    builtins.exec("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'

=== CRW-851-lc-17 | E
--why A new statement after the Ellipsis that continues with a backslash and a newline before the dot of the call.
python3 -c 'import builtins; x = ...
builtins \
.exec("""open(file="{MEMORY}/a",mode="w")""")'
